title: N3 · Unit 13

lessons.title: Identify the actor behind a fictional role
lessons.description: Read a labelled cast and recognise role cues without guessing a person’s identity.
lessons.canDo: Separate a fictional character’s delivery from the actor who actually speaks

lessons.title: Understand the line beyond its ending
lessons.description: Follow the fictional action, interpret wondering and explanation, and check what is still unknown.
lessons.canDo: Recover the underlying message from marked endings and contextual clues

grammar.title: Read a bundle of character cues
grammar.formation: Pronoun/form of address + predicate + sentence ending. Recognise わし/拙者 in labelled fictional roles; identify the actual speaker from the scene.
grammar.explanation: Fiction often bundles pronouns, address forms and endings to suggest a role. わし with じゃ can signal a stylised elder; 拙者 with でござる can signal a stylised samurai. These are recognition cues, not proof of a real person’s age, gender or occupation. One actor can perform several roles. Dialect is a real variety, not incorrect Japanese.
grammar.example: 「わしは道を知っておる」と、老人の役が言う。
grammar.translation: The elder role says, “I know the way.”

examples.ja: 「わしは{道|みち}を{知|し}っておる」と、{老人|ろうじん}の{役|やく}が{言|い}う。
examples.en: The elder role says, “I know the way.”

examples.ja: 「{拙者|せっしゃ}は{門|もん}を{守|まも}る」と、{侍|さむらい}の{役|やく}が{言|い}う。
examples.en: The samurai role says, “I guard the gate.”

examples.ja: {配役|はいやく}を{見|み}ると、{両方|りょうほう}をケンタが{演|えん}じている。
examples.en: The casting shows Kenta performs both roles.

grammar.mistake: Do not answer who actually spoke just by the pronoun. Check the actor label and surrounding scene.

grammar.title: Recognise emphatic ぜ and ぞ
grammar.formation: Plain verb/i-adjective + ぜ/ぞ; noun/na-adjective + だぜ/だぞ. Volitional + ぜ can invite a shared action.
grammar.explanation: ぜ and ぞ add an emphatic, often assertive familiar delivery. They can announce an intention, reaction or warning. Fiction may use them to mark a forceful character, but they are not unique to villains or men. This unit practises understanding labelled script lines; teacher and workplace replies continue to use their appropriate register.
grammar.example: この手紙は俺が届けるぜ。
grammar.translation: I will deliver this letter, I tell you.

examples.ja: この{手紙|てがみ}は{俺|おれ}が{届|とど}けるぜ。
examples.en: I will deliver this letter, I tell you.

examples.ja: {門|もん}の{外|そと}は{危|あぶ}ないぞ。
examples.en: Outside the gate is dangerous, mind you.

examples.ja: この{町|まち}の{英雄|えいゆう}だぞ。
examples.en: That is this town’s hero, you know.

grammar.mistake: Keep noun/na-adjective だ: 英雄だぞ. Do not infer an occupation from ぜ or change the underlying event meaning.

grammar.title: A marked style still carries a meaning
grammar.formation: Plain verb/i-adjective + わ; noun/na-adjective + だわ in the taught script pattern. Plain phrase + かしら; remove plain noun/na-adjective だ before かしら.
grammar.explanation: In a stylised character line, わ can add a marked delivery, while かしら expresses wondering. かしら often sounds feminine in contemporary media, but this is not a rule identifying an actual person. わ also occurs in different regional and casual styles with different intonation. Decode the whole line and context. This unit does not score rising/falling intonation as a verified audio fact.
grammar.example: 門はまだ開いているかしら。
grammar.translation: I wonder whether the gate is still open.

examples.ja: {門|もん}はまだ{開|あ}いているかしら。
examples.en: I wonder whether the gate is still open.

examples.ja: この{手紙|てがみ}は{大切|たいせつ}だわ。
{今日|きょう}は{休|やす}みかしら。
examples.en: I wonder whether today is a day off.

grammar.mistake: かしら is wondering, not a guarantee or completed action. Do not add だ in the taught noun+かしら form or identify gender from わ alone.

grammar.title: のだ connects a statement to its context
grammar.formation: Plain V/i-adjective + のだ/んだ; affirmative noun/na-adjective + なのだ/なんだ. Polite のです/んです.
grammar.explanation: Retrieve the explanatory pattern to give a reason or interpretation connected to the situation. のだ is also common in prose; it is not exclusively an anime or villain ending. Spoken んだ is normal Japanese. Affirmative nouns/na-adjectives require な, while negative じゃない attaches directly. Context supplies the explanatory link; のだ does not make a mistaken claim true.
grammar.example: 道を知らない。初めてこの王国に来たのだ。
grammar.translation: I do not know the way. The thing is, this is my first visit to this kingdom.

examples.ja: {道|みち}を{知|し}らない。{初|はじ}めてこの{王国|おうこく}に{来|き}たのだ。
examples.en: I do not know the way. The thing is, this is my first visit to this kingdom.

examples.ja: {彼|かれ}は{勇者|ゆうしゃ}なのだ。だから{冒険|ぼうけん}に{出|で}る。
examples.en: He is the hero. That is why he goes on the adventure.

examples.ja: {魔法|まほう}は{使|つか}えないんだ。
examples.en: The thing is, I cannot use magic.

grammar.mistake: 勇者なのだ requires な. のだ is explanatory, not an automatic cause marker like ので and not proof that a statement is factual.

grammar.title: Recognise two stylised older copulas
grammar.formation: Fictional elder: N/na-adjective + じゃ (=だ); V/i-adjective + のじゃ for explanatory のだ. Samurai: N/na-adjective + でござる (=である/です here).
grammar.explanation: In this script, noun + じゃ replaces the modern copula だ and noun + でござる creates an older samurai-style statement. A verb is not followed by the same でござる template: the taught noun phrase is 門番でござる. These forms are recognition only. じゃ also has real dialect uses; do not label all users as elderly. Neither is the contraction じゃん or the negative じゃない.
grammar.translation: This is the kingdom’s gate. (stylised elder)

examples.ja: ここは{王国|おうこく}の{門|もん}じゃ。
examples.en: This is the kingdom’s gate. (stylised elder)

examples.ja: {拙者|せっしゃ}は{門番|もんばん}でござる。
この{道|みち}を{進|すす}むのじゃ。
examples.en: You are to follow this road. (stylised elder explanatory instruction)

grammar.mistake: Do not read じゃ as じゃない. Keep で in 門番でござる; recognise the quoted style without using it as a modern business-politeness model.

dialogues.title: Assign roles before reading the script
dialogues.scene: After the previous viewing, Misaki, Kenta and Bao prepare an original short script at home. They label actors before reading. No costume or real-world identity is inferred from the lines.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {前|まえ}の{視聴|しちょう}では{早口|はやくち}の{語尾|ごび}を{聞|き}き{逃|のが}したね。{今日|きょう}は{短|みじか}い{台本|だいほん}を{朗読|ろうどく}しよう。
lines.romaji: Mae no shichō de wa hayakuchi no gobi o kikinogashita ne. Kyō wa mijikai daihon o rōdoku shiyō.
lines.meaning: We missed the rapidly spoken endings in the earlier viewing. Today let us read a short script aloud.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: まず{人物|じんぶつ}と{配役|はいやく}を{確認|かくにん}しよう。{僕|ぼく}は{侍|さむらい}と{老人|ろうじん}、ミサキは{姫|ひめ}、バオは{忍者|にんじゃ}だね。
lines.romaji: Mazu jinbutsu to haiyaku o kakunin shiyō. Boku wa samurai to rōjin, Misaki wa hime, Bao wa ninja da ne.
lines.meaning: First let us check the characters and casting. I have the samurai and elder, Misaki the princess, and Bao the ninja.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {主役|しゅやく}と{脇役|わきやく}の{場面|ばめん}は{別|べつ}だね。{仮装|かそう}をしなくても、{誰|だれ}がどの{役|やく}を{演|えん}じるか{分|わ}かるようにしよう。
lines.romaji: Shuyaku to wakiyaku no bamen wa betsu da ne. Kasō o shinakute mo, dare ga dono yaku o enjiru ka wakaru yō ni shiyō.
lines.meaning: The leading and supporting roles have separate scenes. Let us make clear who performs each role even without costumes.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {人称|にんしょう}の{言葉|ことば}や{呼称|こしょう}、{口癖|くちぐせ}も{手掛|てが}かりになるよ。でも{役|やく}と{演|えん}じる{人|ひと}は{同|おな}じではないね。
lines.romaji: Ninshō no kotoba ya koshō, kuchiguse mo tegakari ni naru yo. Demo yaku to enjiru hito wa onaji de wa nai ne.
lines.meaning: Person words, forms of address and habitual phrases can be clues too. But the role and the person performing it are not the same.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {侍|さむらい}の{台詞|せりふ}を{読|よ}むよ。「{拙者|せっしゃ}は{門番|もんばん}でござる」。{武士|ぶし}の{役|やく}だけど、{僕|ぼく}は{今|いま}の{学生|がくせい}だよ。
lines.romaji: Samurai no serifu o yomu yo. Sessha wa monban de gozaru. Bushi no yaku da kedo, boku wa ima no gakusei da yo.
lines.meaning: I will read the samurai line: “I am the gatekeeper.” It is a warrior role, but I am a present-day student.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {次|つぎ}は{忍者|にんじゃ}の{台詞|せりふ}だね。「この{手紙|てがみ}は{俺|おれ}が{届|とど}けるぜ」。{普通|ふつう}に{言|い}うなら「{私|わたし}が{届|とど}けます」だ。
lines.romaji: Tsugi wa ninja no serifu da ne. Kono tegami wa ore ga todokeru ze. Futsū ni iu nara watashi ga todokemasu da.
lines.meaning: Next is the ninja line: “I will deliver this letter.” In ordinary polite speech it would be “I will deliver it.”

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {老人|ろうじん}の{台詞|せりふ}も{僕|ぼく}が{読|よ}むよ。「ここは{町|まち}の{門|もん}じゃ」。{役|やく}が{変|か}わっても、{話|はな}しているのは{僕|ぼく}だね。
lines.romaji: Rōjin no serifu mo boku ga yomu yo. Koko wa machi no mon ja. Yaku ga kawatte mo, hanashite iru no wa boku da ne.
lines.meaning: I will read the elder line too: “This is the town’s gate.” Even though the role changes, I am still the one speaking.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {方言|ほうげん}と{役|やく}の{言葉|ことば}は{重|かさ}なることもあるよ。{標準語|ひょうじゅんご}で{言|い}い{直|なお}して{意味|いみ}も{確認|かくにん}しよう。
lines.romaji: Hōgen to yaku no kotoba wa kasanaru koto mo aru yo. Hyōjungo de iinaoshite imi mo kakunin shiyō.
lines.meaning: Dialect and character speech can overlap. Let us rephrase in standard language and check the meaning too.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {音量|おんりょう}は{今|いま}のままで{聞|き}こえるよ。{予告|よこく}と{同|おな}じように、{分|わ}からなければ{巻|ま}き{戻|もど}そう。
lines.romaji: Onryō wa ima no mama de kikoeru yo. Yokoku to onaji yō ni, wakaranakereba makimodosō.
lines.meaning: I can hear at the current volume. As with the preview, let us rewind if we do not understand.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {話|はな}し{言葉|ことば}の{練習|れんしゅう}だけど、{台本|だいほん}を{仕事|しごと}の{返事|へんじ}にそのまま{使|つか}うわけではないね。
lines.romaji: Hanashikotoba no renshū da kedo, daihon o shigoto no henji ni sono mama tsukau wake de wa nai ne.
lines.meaning: This is spoken-language practice, but we are not using the script unchanged for replies at work.

dialogues.title: A fictional gate; real actors
dialogues.scene: Misaki, Kenta and Bao continue the same original script, quoting roles assigned in the first scene. The fictional elder delays departure until tomorrow; the actors decide to check the message before continuing.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: この{物語|ものがたり}の{王国|おうこく}は{架空|かくう}だね。{姫|ひめ}の{台詞|せりふ}を{読|よ}むよ。「{門|もん}はまだ{開|あ}いているかしら」。
lines.romaji: Kono monogatari no ōkoku wa kakū da ne. Hime no serifu o yomu yo. Mon wa mada aite iru kashira.
lines.meaning: This story’s kingdom is fictional. I will read the princess’s line: “I wonder whether the gate is still open.”

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {老人|ろうじん}の{台詞|せりふ}だよ。「{門|もん}は{閉|し}まっておる。{冒険|ぼうけん}に{出|で}るのは{明日|あした}じゃ」。{今日|きょう}ではないね。
lines.romaji: Rōjin no serifu da yo. Mon wa shimatte oru. Bōken ni deru no wa ashita ja. Kyō de wa nai ne.
lines.meaning: This is the elder’s line: “The gate is closed. The adventure starts tomorrow.” It is not today.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {忍者|にんじゃ}の{台詞|せりふ}は「{手紙|てがみ}を{渡|わた}すまで{待|ま}つぞ」。{最後|さいご}を{強調|きょうちょう}しても、{渡|わた}したという{意味|いみ}にはならないね。
lines.romaji: Ninja no serifu wa tegami o watasu made matsu zo. Saigo o kyōchō shite mo, watashita to iu imi ni wa naranai ne.
lines.meaning: The ninja’s line is “I will wait until I hand over the letter.” Emphasising the end does not mean it has already been handed over.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {続|つづ}きは「この{手紙|てがみ}は{大切|たいせつ}だわ」。{語尾|ごび}だけで{現実|げんじつ}の{人|ひと}の{性別|せいべつ}や{年齢|ねんれい}を{決|き}めないようにしよう。
lines.romaji: Tsuzuki wa kono tegami wa taisetsu da wa. Gobi dake de genjitsu no hito no seibetsu ya nenrei o kimenai yō ni shiyō.
lines.meaning: The next line is “This letter is important.” Let us avoid deciding a real person’s gender or age from an ending alone.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {特徴|とくちょう}は{手掛|てが}かりで、{答|こた}えそのものではないね。{尊大|そんだい}な{話|はな}し{方|かた}だから{悪役|あくやく}だ、とも{限|かぎ}らない。
lines.romaji: Tokuchō wa tegakari de, kotae sono mono de wa nai ne. Sondai na hanashikata da kara akuyaku da, to mo kagiranai.
lines.meaning: A characteristic is a clue, not the answer itself. Haughty speech does not necessarily make a character a villain either.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: この{場面|ばめん}では{誰|だれ}が{英雄|えいゆう}か、まだ{分|わ}からないね。{勇者|ゆうしゃ}なのだ、という{説明|せつめい}も{筋書|すじが}きの{中|なか}で{確|たし}かめよう。
lines.romaji: Kono bamen de wa dare ga eiyū ka, mada wakaranai ne. Yūsha na no da, to iu setsumei mo sujigaki no naka de tashikameyō.
lines.meaning: In this scene we do not yet know who the hero is. Let us check “he is the hero” within the plot too.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {魔法|まほう}を{使|つか}えないのだ、という{台詞|せりふ}の{理由|りゆう}は、まだ{練習|れんしゅう}していないからだね。{言葉|ことば}の{解釈|かいしゃく}は、{前後|ぜんご}も{聞|き}いてからしよう。
lines.romaji: Mahō o tsukaenai no da, to iu serifu no riyū wa, mada renshū shite inai kara da ne. Kotoba no kaishaku wa, zengo mo kiite kara shiyō.
lines.meaning: The reason for the line “the thing is, I cannot use magic” is that the character has not practised yet. Let us interpret the words after listening to what comes before and after too.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {誇張|こちょう}された{語尾|ごび}だけでなく、くだけた{返事|へんじ}も{残|のこ}しておこう。{結末|けつまつ}は{今|いま}の{台本|だいほん}にはないよ。
lines.romaji: Kochō sareta gobi dake de naku, kudaketa henji mo nokoshite okō. Ketsumatsu wa ima no daihon ni wa nai yo.
lines.meaning: Let us keep the informal replies too, not just the exaggerated endings. The ending is not in the current script.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: うっかり{先|さき}に{進|すす}まず、{合図|あいず}があったら{同|おな}じ{場面|ばめん}に{戻|もど}そう。{主役|しゅやく}と{脇役|わきやく}の{台詞|せりふ}も{両方|りょうほう}{聞|き}こう。
lines.romaji: Ukkari saki ni susumazu, aizu ga attara onaji bamen ni modosō. Shuyaku to wakiyaku no serifu mo ryōhō kikō.
lines.meaning: Rather than inadvertently going ahead, let us return to the same scene on a signal. Let us listen to both the lead and supporting lines.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {次|つぎ}の{視聴|しちょう}では{台詞|せりふ}の{意味|いみ}と{話|はな}した{人|ひと}を{別々|べつべつ}にメモしよう。{今日|きょう}は、この{手紙|てがみ}の{内容|ないよう}を{確認|かくにん}して{終|お}わりにするね。
lines.romaji: Tsugi no shichō de wa serifu no imi to hanashita hito o betsubetsu ni memo shiyō. Kyō wa, kono tegami no naiyō o kakunin shite owari ni suru ne.
lines.meaning: In the next viewing, let us note the line’s meaning and actual speaker separately. Today we will finish after checking this letter’s contents.

readings.title: Casting notes distinguish actors and roles
paragraphs: ケンタとバオへ。{今日|きょう}の{朗読|ろうどく}の{配役|はいやく}を{残|のこ}しておくね。ケンタが{侍|さむらい}と{老人|ろうじん}、バオが{忍者|にんじゃ}、{私|わたし}が{姫|ひめ}を{演|えん}じた。{仮装|かそう}はしていない。{人物|じんぶつ}の{年齢|ねんれい}は、{演|えん}じた{人|ひと}の{年齢|ねんれい}とは{別|べつ}だよ。
{架空|かくう}の{王国|おうこく}の{門|もん}は{閉|し}まっていて、{冒険|ぼうけん}に{出|で}るのは{明日|あした}だと{老人|ろうじん}の{役|やく}が{言|い}った。{忍者|にんじゃ}は{手紙|てがみ}を{渡|わた}すまで{待|ま}つと{言|い}っただけで、まだ{渡|わた}していない。{結末|けつまつ}はこの{台本|だいほん}には{書|か}いていない。
{語尾|ごび}の{特徴|とくちょう}や{口癖|くちぐせ}は{解釈|かいしゃく}の{手掛|てが}かりだけど、{現実|げんじつ}の{性別|せいべつ}や{年齢|ねんれい}を{決|き}めるものではない。{次|つぎ}の{視聴|しちょう}では{場面|ばめん}の{前後|ぜんご}も{聞|き}くね。ミサキ

exercises.prompt: Which two roles does Kenta perform?
exercises.explain: Kenta explicitly assigns himself 侍と老人; Misaki and Bao have the other two roles.

exercises.prompt: How will they make the roles clear without costumes?
options: Label which actor performs each role
Assume an ending reveals the real age
Use workplace replies unchanged as script lines
exercises.explain: Bao asks to make 誰がどの役を演じる clear even without 仮装.

exercises.prompt: Why did Misaki suggest reading a short script?
options: They missed fast endings in the earlier viewing
They had already completed the sequel
exercises.explain: Misaki recalls 早口の語尾を聞き逃した; the script is their home practice.

exercises.context: Form practice: keep the noun copula before the named emphatic ending ぜ.
exercises.line: この{人物|じんぶつ}は{武士|ぶし}＿＿ぜ。
exercises.explain: Noun+だぜ. The emphasis does not identify who actually reads the line.

exercises.context: Form practice: add the named emphatic ぞ directly to the plain verb, without a noun copula.
exercises.line: {侍|さむらい}が{手紙|てがみ}を{渡|わた}す＿＿。
exercises.explain: Plain verb+ぞ, not 渡すだぞ.

exercises.context: Your friend missed the meaning. Offer to rephrase in standard language and listen again.
exercises.line: {意味|いみ}を{聞|き}き{逃|のが}した。
options: {標準語|ひょうじゅんご}で{言|い}い{直|なお}して、もう{一度|いちど}{聞|き}こう。
{聞|き}き{逃|のが}したなら、もう{全部|ぜんぶ}{分|わ}かったんだね。
{意味|いみ}は{気|き}にせず、{音量|おんりょう}だけ{見|み}よう。
exercises.explain: Rephrasing and replay respond to missed meaning; the others falsely assume understanding or dismiss it.

exercises.line: {侍|さむらい}の{台詞|せりふ}を{読|よ}むよ。「{拙者|せっしゃ}は{門番|もんばん}でござる」。{武士|ぶし}の{役|やく}だけど、{僕|ぼく}は{今|いま}の{学生|がくせい}だよ。
exercises.prompt: Who actually reads the samurai line in this scene?
exercises.explain: The entire recorded line belongs to Kenta. His performed role is a samurai, but his real identity remains the student Kenta.

exercises.prompt: When does the fictional elder say the adventure begins?
exercises.explain: 冒険に出るのは明日じゃ explicitly says tomorrow; Kenta clarifies 今日ではない.

exercises.prompt: What does the ninja’s line establish about the letter?
options: He will wait until handing it over; it is not yet delivered
exercises.explain: 待つぞ announces waiting until delivery, not completed delivery. Bao explicitly distinguishes the meanings.

exercises.context: Form practice: attach the named wondering かしら to a noun without だ.
exercises.line: {明日|あした}の{朗読|ろうどく}はお{休|やす}み＿＿。
exercises.explain: 休み+かしら in this taught wondering pattern; it does not assert the answer.

exercises.context: Form practice: use the named explanatory のだ after the affirmative noun 勇者.
exercises.line: {彼|かれ}は{勇者|ゆうしゃ}＿＿のだ。
exercises.explain: Affirmative noun+なのだ, not 勇者だのだ.

exercises.context: Recognition/form practice: complete the fictional elder’s positive noun statement with the named older copula じゃ.
exercises.line: ここは{王国|おうこく}の{門|もん}＿＿。
exercises.explain: Noun+じゃ is the stylised copula here. It is neither affirmative じゃん nor negative じゃない.

exercises.context: A friend asks whether an ending alone identifies a real person. Explain that the surrounding scene matters.
exercises.line: {語尾|ごび}だけで、{誰|だれ}か{分|わ}かる？
options: {語尾|ごび}は{手掛|てが}かりだけど、{場面|ばめん}の{前後|ぜんご}も{聞|き}いて{解釈|かいしゃく}しよう。
{語尾|ごび}だけで{現実|げんじつ}の{年齢|ねんれい}が{必|かなら}ず{分|わ}かるよ。
{台本|だいほん}には{人物|じんぶつ}がいないよ。
exercises.explain: The first treats the ending as a clue in context; the others contradict the scene.

exercises.line: この{物語|ものがたり}の{王国|おうこく}は{架空|かくう}だね。{姫|ひめ}の{台詞|せりふ}を{読|よ}むよ。「{門|もん}はまだ{開|あ}いているかしら」。
exercises.prompt: Who actually wonders about the open gate while reading the princess’s line?
exercises.explain: The scene and exact recorded line label Misaki as the actor reading the princess. The ending itself does not prove the actor’s identity.

exercises.meaning: The thing is, I cannot use magic. Use the explanatory のだ.
exercises.explain: The negative plain verb 使えない takes のだ directly; noun/na-adjective な is not used here.

exercises.prompt: Who performed the elder role in the casting notes?
exercises.explain: The first paragraph assigns Kenta both the samurai and elder roles.

exercises.prompt: According to the message, what is the delivery status?
options: The ninja has not handed over the letter yet
The elder has torn it up
exercises.explain: The second paragraph explicitly says まだ渡していない.

exercises.prompt: What will Misaki check in the next viewing?
options: What comes before and after the scene
exercises.explain: The last paragraph says 場面の前後も聞く; the ending is not in the script.

watch.prompt: Optionally save a character line from your own clip. Note the literal message, role cue, actual speaker and surrounding action. Do not use fictional speech as a model for every real interaction.
